You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/** + components/portal/**. Static assets in public/**.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do not read .env* files. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-03-assets.md (Write tool). Exhaustive, factual, cite repo-relative file paths, use tables, mark uncertain items UNVERIFIED.

YOUR AUDIT: VISUAL ASSET INVENTORY with a KEEP / REWORK / REPLACE / REMOVE verdict per asset. The owner's rule: the default for DECORATIVE assets is REPLACE; nothing gets recycled just because it exists; the logo/wordmark and legitimately-licensed game artwork are the main KEEP candidates; screenshots are never an asset source.
Produce:
1. public/** inventory: every image/svg/video/font/ico/og-image file (use find + du + identify/file for dimensions and format). Group by folder (logos, game art/heroes/posters, illustrations, backgrounds, icons, og images, favicons, app/one-click icons, region/flag images, screenshots, misc). For each: path, dimensions, size, format, what it depicts (open the image if not obvious — you can Read PNG/JPG/SVG files), where it is referenced (grep the src for its filename; note UNREFERENCED files), and a verdict KEEP/REWORK/REPLACE/REMOVE with one-line reason. For game artwork, note whether it looks like official artwork vs generated, and any licensing notes you can find (README, LICENSE, comments, a games manifest).
2. Logo / wordmark treatments: every variant of the Nxeon logo (svg/png, colour variants, favicon, og image, email logo, loading logo), where used, inconsistencies.
3. Inline decorative graphics inside components (grep for <svg in components/customer, components/portal, app/dashboard and also app/ marketing pages if they share components): glows, blobs, orbs, grids, mesh gradients, noise, particle/starfield effects, hero backdrops, gradient text — list each with file:line and verdict.
4. CSS-generated decoration: background-image utilities, radial-gradient/conic-gradient in globals.css or components, animated backgrounds, blur orbs — list with verdict.
5. Illustrations for empty states / onboarding / success / error — what exists, style consistency, verdict.
6. Game catalogue visuals: how games are represented (which manifest/lib file lists games, image fields, aspect ratios, per-game hero/poster/logo), count of games, missing images, mixed aspect ratios.
7. One-click app / OS / region imagery: what's used for Ubuntu/Debian/Docker/WordPress/etc. and for regions (flags? maps?), source and verdict.
8. Email templates' imagery (if there are email templates in lib/ or emails/) — list only, verdict.
9. Summary table: counts per verdict, and the short list of what the new asset library must provide (categories + rough counts), without designing them.
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~10-line summary with counts per verdict.
